USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

mayo — pattern 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A high-energy elbow injury causes a displaced simple olecranon fracture with associated ulnohumeral instability and dislocation. Imaging shows no comminution of the olecranon fragment. Which subtype incorporates the unstable joint rather than treating the injury as a stable displaced fracture? Which Mayo olecranon fracture subtype best describes these findings?

  1. Type IIIB
  2. Type IA
  3. Type IB
  4. Type IIA
  5. Type IIIA
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Type IIIA

Type IIIA: A displaced, noncomminuted olecranon fracture with ulnohumeral instability.

Understanding the options

Type IIIA
Type IIIA: A displaced, noncomminuted olecranon fracture with ulnohumeral instability.
Type IIIB
Type IIIB describes a displaced, comminuted olecranon fracture with ulnohumeral instability. The case instead matches Type IIIA.
Type IA
Type IA describes a nondisplaced, noncomminuted olecranon fracture. The case instead matches Type IIIA.
Type IB
Type IB describes a nondisplaced, comminuted olecranon fracture. The case instead matches Type IIIA.
Type IIA
Type IIA describes a displaced, noncomminuted olecranon fracture with a stable ulnohumeral joint. The case instead matches Type IIIA.
